narratives.Overview:
## Summary

AppSec scan on **`36280b61`** (post-**#3545**) found two **HIGH** UAT Shell classification residuals, one **MEDIUM** incomplete mint-path fix, and one **MEDIUM** release-pipeline symlink write.

Under active UAT, further write-capable binaries still classify empty / unclassifiable and **allow** write-shaped Shell. That path can plant a forged `.deft/authz` grant or a regular-file `.deft-directive-disable` kill-switch. Separately, residual Shell writers can still forge `.deft/approved-scope` while Write is denied, so the #3410 / #3421 / #3529 / #3545 mint gate is incomplete. Independently, CHANGELOG promotion in the release pipeline follows an in-tree leaf symlink (`assertProjectionContained` only) and can overwrite a diverted tracked file under operator release credentials.

These residuals use dest forms that **#3545's harvest does not cover** (`qjs` / `quickjs` / `jsc` / `d8` / `hermes` / `boa`; `ipython` / `xonsh` / `jython` / `circuitpython`; `csi` / `dotnet-script`; `chrome` / `chromium` / `wkhtmltopdf` / `weasyprint` / `qpdf`; `lame` / `binwalk`; `buildah` / `ctr`; `webpack` / `parcel` / `uv` / `pyinstaller` / `sphinx` / `cargo` / `ldc2` / `mlton`; `lipo` / `pkgutil` / `defaults` / `eu-objcopy`).

**Repo / tip:** `deftai/directive` @ `36280b61`
**Primary code:** `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`; CHANGELOG sink: `packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts`
**Attacker model:** Agent under **active UAT** with PreToolUse Shell hooks (findings 1-3); operator-credentialed `task release` write (finding 4)

**Already denied after #3545 (do not re-report):** `rubyN` / `jruby` / `pypy`, Perl `write_file` / `spew` / `open F,">"`, `make DESTDIR=`, `dpkg -x`, `fromdos` / `todos`, `emacsclient` / `pico`, `pdftk` / `gs`, `npx degit`, `composer`, `ddrescue` / `dc3dd` / `sg_dd`, `darcs --repodir=`, `cp`, `python3`. Contrast: those peers remain settings-denied.

**Siblings, not duplicates:** open **#3593** tracks a *different* post-#3545 harvest (`raku` / `graalpy` / `crystal` / `groovy` / `clojure` / `micropython` / `jar` / `gsed` / `helm` / `s3cmd` / `sbase-cp`) plus MCP write routing and a migrate agents-header symlink sink. Open **#3626** tracks `ffmpeg` / `sox` / Lisp / `llvm-objcopy` / `zig` / `.NET` emitters. Open **#3728** tracks `erl` / `sage` / CAS / `tcpdump` / `screen` / `joe` / `guestfish` / `adb` / `dmd` / `vbc`. Do **not** close this as a duplicate of those, and do **not** reopen #3545. Finding 4 is a **distinct sink** of the #2912 class (sibling of #3593 finding 5, not the same write site).

## Findings

### 1. HIGH — UAT residual after #3545: qjs / ipython / csi / chrome / lame / webpack / … still plant `.deft/authz` grants

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` |
| **Attacker** | Agent under active UAT with PreToolUse Shell hooks |
| **Input** | Residual writers whose dest is **not** covered by the #3545 harvest: `qjs` / `quickjs` / `jsc` / `d8` / `hermes` / `boa`; `ipython` / `xonsh` / `jython` / `circuitpython`; `csi` / `dotnet-script`; `chrome` / `chromium` / `wkhtmltopdf` / `weasyprint` / `qpdf`; `lame` / `binwalk`; `buildah` / `ctr`; `webpack` / `parcel` / `uv` / `pyinstaller` / `sphinx` / `cargo` / `ldc2` / `mlton`; `lipo` / `pkgutil` / `defaults` / `eu-objcopy` when dest mentions `.deft/authz` |
| **Path** | Residual bins classify `[]` → `shell-op-unclassifiable` **allow** → forged operator-cli grant JSON → empty `activeGrantIds` activates human-origin grants → Write / push / PR / merge unlock. Contrast: `cp` / `python3` targeting the same dest **deny** / `authz-grant-missing`. |
| **Impact** | Complete residual bypass of Wave 1 UAT human-approval after #3545 |
| **Fix** | Classify these dest writers when the path mentions `.deft/authz`. Under UAT, **fail-closed** on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell. Do **not** stop at named-peer allowlists. `cp` / `python3` already deny. |

### 2. HIGH — UAT residual after #3545: same writer class still plants `.deft-directive-disable`

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` |
| **Attacker** | Agent under active UAT |
| **Input** | Same residual class targeting `.deft-directive-disable` as a regular file |
| **Path** | classify `[]` → Shell **allow** → plant kill-switch → subsequent tools `allow` / `directive-disabled` (`detectDeftDirectiveDisable.active`, #3039) |
| **Impact** | Immediate complete Directive gate bypass for the rest of the session |
| **Fix** | Same classify extensions for kill-switch basenames (`.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive`). Mirror the authz fail-closed posture from finding (1). |

### 3. MEDIUM — Incomplete #3545: residual Shell writers still forge `.deft/approved-scope` while Write is denied

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` |
| **Attacker** | Agent under active UAT |
| **Input** | Same residual dest writers targeting `.deft/approved-scope/<plan-id>.json` after Write is denied for the same path (Write denied; residual writers above still allow; contrast `cp` denied) |
| **Path** | Write denies the mint artifact; residual Shell classify misses the dest form → **allow** → forged provenance approval without `#3110` human-presence mint |
| **Impact** | Bypasses #3410 / #3421 / #3529 / #3545 mint gate via Write / Shell asymmetry |
| **Fix** | Extend approved-scope Shell classify to the same residual dest writers as findings (1) and (2). |

### 4. MEDIUM — Release pipeline CHANGELOG write follows in-tree leaf symlink (`assertProjectionContained` only)

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Location** | `packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts` (Step 6 CHANGELOG promotion, ~424-425) |
| **Attacker** | Operator-credentialed `task release` / pipeline write (no UAT grant required) |
| **Input** | Tracked `CHANGELOG.md` replaced by an in-tree leaf symlink to a victim (e.g. `package.json`). `assertProjectionContained` allows the in-tree target; `assertWriteTargetSafe` would refuse. |
| **Path** | `assertProjectionContained(projectRoot, changelogPath)` then `writeFile` → `writeFileSync` follows the symlink and overwrites the victim with promoted CHANGELOG text. Init-deposit #2912 closed this class for deposit writes; migrate agents-header is tracked on #3593 finding 5. This sink is the release CHANGELOG writer. |
| **Impact** | Integrity corruption of diverted tracked files under operator release credentials |
| **Fix** | Route CHANGELOG write through `assertWriteTargetSafe` / `containedWrite` before `writeFileSync` (mirror init-deposit #2912). Do not keep `writeFileSync` on a projection-contained path that may be a symlink. |

### Comment by @ZaenKai (2026-08-31T14:32:41Z)

Consumer data point on the shell-residual surface, engine 0.107.0 / content 0.107.0. Posting here rather than on #3545, which is closed.

The `protected-files` hook is bypassable through the shell, and separately has no approval path. Both halves matter, and the second drives the first.

The hook guards a declared protected set. `Write`/`Edit` are intercepted; shell writes are not — `python -c`, `cp` and similar reach the same paths unchecked. That alone is the residual this issue tracks.

The compounding half: there is no sanctioned way to edit a protected file *with* approval. A consumer whose operator has explicitly authorised a specific change to a specific protected file has no verb that records that authorisation and permits the write. The only paths available are (a) don't make the change, or (b) use the shell. So the missing approval path actively pushes correct, authorised work onto the bypass route — which then also trains agents that the bypass exists.

A concrete instance of the same shape, from this session, on a file that is not in the protected set but is gated the same way: `plan.policy.valueFeedback.upstreamPrompt` has no CLI setter — `policy:enable-value-feedback` writes the master flag and leaves the sub-flag at its `false` default. The only route is a hand edit of `PROJECT-DEFINITION`, which the scope write fence denies when `xbrief/active/` is empty. An operator-authorised policy change had no non-shell route until the fence happened to admit the write on a later attempt. Same structure: a legitimate, authorised edit with no first-class door.

Suggested, if not already covered by #3545: an explicit, audited approval verb — a recorded operator grant scoped to one file and one change, consumed once — so that authorised edits have a first-class route and the shell residual stops being the only door.

## 1. blocks-the-design — the fail-closed clause already landed, and it landed without the harvest

`bf9d26c8c` — *fix(hooks,security): fail closed on unknown writes to UAT-protected dests (#4449)*, closing #4188 — is in the tree at the dispatch SHA and postdates the scan. Its own commit body: "Unknown Shell bins whose last dest-of-write is `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft/approved-scope/**`, `.deft-directive-disable`, or `.no-deft-directive` classify unknown and UAT-deny grant-immune… **Does not grow dest-flag or write-bin catalogs.**"

Mechanism: `classify.ts:3993-3998` adds `unknown`; `evaluate.ts:323-330` denies `unknown` under an active UAT lease *before* `findCoveringGrant` is ever reached.

Failure mode if bound as written: an implementer works the HIGH acceptance block, adds ~33 bin names, and ships regression tests asserting deny for `hermes` / `webpack` / `qpdf` / `lame` / `jsc` — all of which already deny. The harvest buys nothing measurable, the AC checkboxes all go green, and the actual residual (findings 3 and 4 below) stays open behind a satisfied acceptance list.

Disposition consequence: the evidence table is stale and the HIGH block cannot be bound as the statement of work. Re-measure against `9a28d509` first; whatever is left is a different, much smaller issue.

## 2. blocks-the-design — the harvest, as the AC words it, downgrades the control

The AC says these bins must "classify as **settings deny**". `settings` and `unknown` are not the same verdict. `classify.ts:3990-3992` states the split in-source: "Dest-flag plants stay settings (grantable). Zip first-positional and unknown-argv0 last-positional dests emit unknown (grant-immune under UAT)." The emit is guarded by `!found.has("settings")`.

So for every bin currently reaching `unknown` — `webpack`, `qpdf`, `lame`, `jsc`, measured above — cataloguing it to satisfy this AC moves it out of the grant-immune branch (`evaluate.ts:323`) and into the branch that a covering human-origin grant can satisfy (`evaluate.ts:345`). Under an attacker model whose whole objective is forging grants, trading a grant-immune deny for a grant-satisfiable one is a net loss, and its size depends entirely on grant scoping that this issue never examines.

Disposition consequence: "classify as settings deny" is the wrong target verdict. If a bin must be named at all, the AC has to say which of the two classes it lands in and why.

## 3. blocks-the-design — the landed control is positional; one trailing operand defeats it

`hasProtectedUnprovenReadOnlyDestOfWrite` (`classify.ts:2429-2452`) tests only `lastNonFlagWord` (`classify.ts:2349-2359`). Measured:

| command | measured |
|---|---|
| `webpack --output-path .deft/authz/grants` | `["unknown"]` → deny |
| `webpack --output-path .deft/authz/grants --mode production` | `[]` → **allow** |
| `lame in.wav .deft-directive-disable` | `["unknown"]` → deny |
| `lame in.wav .deft-directive-disable --quiet 1` | `[]` → **allow** |
| `qpdf --empty --pages . -- .deft/approved-scope/p.json` | `["unknown"]` → deny |
| `qpdf --empty --pages . -- .deft/approved-scope/p.json extra` | `[]` → **allow** |
| `chrome --headless --print-to-pdf=.deft/authz/grants/x.json` | `[]` → **allow** (dest is last, but `=`-joined into a flag) |

Appending one flag-less word — including the value of an otherwise-ignored trailing option — moves the protected path off the last position and the command falls back to `shell-op-unclassifiable` allow. The `--flag=DEST` form never reaches the check at all, because `lastNonFlagWord` skips anything starting with `-`.

Failure mode: agent under active UAT runs `lame in.wav .deft-directive-disable --quiet 1`, plants the kill-switch, and every subsequent tool returns `allow` / `directive-disabled` per `detectDeftDirectiveDisable.active` (#3039). Same bin, same dest, same session — the only difference from the denied form is two trailing words.

Disposition consequence: what is implemented is *fail-closed on an unclassifiable last-positional protected dest*, not "fail-closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell." The issue's AC wording ("Prefer fail-closed on unclassifiable **write-shaped** Shell under UAT") can be marked satisfied by the already-landed control while this bypass stands. This is the finding that should carry the story; the bin list is not.

## 4. blocks-the-design — an argv0 skip list inside the general control

`argv0HasExistingDestGrammar` (`classify.ts:2330-2347`) returns `true` for `TEST_BINS` (`classify.ts:108`) = `vitest`, `pytest`, `cargo`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `task`, and `hasProtectedUnprovenReadOnlyDestOfWrite` skips any segment whose argv0 matches. Those seven bins have no dest grammar, so they fall through to `[]`. Measured, identical grammar:

| command | measured |
|---|---|
| `notabin build --out-dir .deft-directive-disable` | `["unknown"]` → deny |
| `task build --out-dir .deft-directive-disable` | `[]` → **allow** |
| `cargo build --out-dir .deft/authz/grants` | `[]` → **allow** |
